title: Fix multi-page still plateauing: hop progression judged by difference, not length; landing wait judged by progress+stability, not a guessed delay
action: User field-test finding (2026-07-28), after cell -6 still plateaued for them: live re-test on 2 real idle panes with the deployed cell -6 build showed depth 1..4 all returning the SAME length per pane (worse than cell -6's own earlier partial result) despite 150ms settle. Raw manual PageUp testing with a generous 1s delay between hops (bypassing herdr-go entirely) reproduced the true root cause: on a real Claude Code pane, successive PageUp hops behave like a pager advancing by a fixed viewport, NOT a strictly-growing buffer -- baseline 4726 chars, hop1 4887, hop2 4462 (SHORTER than hop1!), hop3 5411 -- non-monotonic but genuinely different content each time. is_richer (length comparison) is the wrong invariant for hop-to-hop progression: a shorter-but-different page was being silently discarded as 'not richer' and the loop gave up. Two changes: (1) hop progression (and the restore-wait) now judged by simple content INEQUALITY (`r.text != before.text`), never is_richer/length -- is_richer is kept ONLY for the original NativeScrollback-vs-Visible pre-check, where a strict superset/tail-match by construction (D2) genuinely is the right test. (2) Landing/settling itself no longer waits for a fixed guessed delay (INTER_HOP_SETTLE, tried 150ms, still insufficient for some real sessions) -- replaced with `wait_until_progressed_and_stable`, a generic two-phase poll (wait for ANY progress per the caller's own predicate, then wait for 2 consecutive identical reads = genuinely stopped changing) shared by both the escalation and restore waits, bounded by one shared STABILITY_READ_ATTEMPTS/INTERVAL budget (10 attempts x 50ms). Live re-verified on both previously-plateauing panes: every depth 1-4 now returns a distinct length (w3:p6: 8680/8543/8972/8166; w8:p1: 8247/7499/7157/7919) -- no more plateau.

truths: hop-to-hop progression is judged by content inequality, never by is_richer/length
is_richer is used only for the NativeScrollback-vs-Visible pre-check, not for hop advancement or restore
the landing wait combines 'has it progressed at all' with 'has it stopped changing' (stability) sharing one bounded attempt budget, replacing any fixed guessed settle delay
requesting depths 1..N on a real multi-page-capable pane returns genuinely distinct content per depth, not a plateau

artifacts.substantive: wait_until_progressed_and_stable() replaces the separate escalation-read-loop/INTER_HOP_SETTLE/restore-read-loop; hop and restore completion both use content inequality as the progress predicate; STABILITY_READ_ATTEMPTS/INTERVAL replace ESCALATION_READ_ATTEMPTS/INTERVAL/INTER_HOP_SETTLE

key_links: is_richer's only remaining caller is the NativeScrollback-vs-Visible pre-check; every hop/restore completion check now uses plain != instead
prohibitions: no change to the always-restore-to-live guarantee
